Hi Alex —

Thanks again for taking the time this morning. Quick recap from our call:
- FinPath use case: customer support automation + next-best-action for agents (real-time latency requirements).
- Data flow: embeddings for ticket history + context window, hosted inference preferred but exploring Dedicated for peak hours.
- Success metrics: 30% reduction in agent handling time, sub-300ms p95 runtime for short responses.

Next steps I suggested:
1) 60–75 minute technical demo / architecture deep dive with your platform and security teams (we'll cover integration patterns, latency/throughput, and quantization/hosting options).
2) Mutual action plan & security packet exchange so procurement and security can validate controls.

Proposed times (PST):
- Tue Dec 1, 10:00–11:15
- Wed Dec 2, 14:00–15:15

If either of those work, I’ll loop in our security lead (Neha) and SE (Dev) and send a calendar invite. I’ve attached a one-pager and the mutual action plan draft to speed procurement review.

Attachments: Product_Overview.pdf (one-pager), Mutual_Action_Plan_FINPATH.xlsx

Thanks —

Marissa / Alex / Team —

Thanks for looping me in. I reviewed the security packet quickly; a few items procurement/security will commonly ask for during our intake:
- Data retention defaults and how customer-configured retention is enforced (section 3 in the packet covers this; can you confirm the typical retention window for embeddings and logs?)
- For SOC 2 deliverables: we typically request the Type II report and the associated controls matrix. If you can share a secure link (NDA first if required), that helps speed internal review.
- Network/egress: if you plan to use Dedicated/on-prem vs hosted, note the firewall/IP allowlist requirements and any peering options. Dev, can you propose the simplest integration pattern for FinPath?

Alex/Priya — if Wed Dec 2, 14:00 PST is the preferred slot, I’ll join and bring baseline questions so we can identify any gating items before procurement issues an SOW/PO.
